A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MSEarth, retaining the same benchmark tasks and core construction pipeline. All 30 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including appendices, figures, and tables, support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, caption-input ablations, compute-scaling experiments, and expert assessments of generated questions.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds post-training evaluations, human validation of OE-Eval, expert performance comparisons, and further reasoning experiments.

M1.justification: V2 adds a model-training branch absent from v1: instruction tuning for captioning and open-ended QA, and GRPO for MCQs, applied to Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Intern-S1-mini (Section 4.1). The refined-caption and voting pipeline remains, with selective training-data sampling and an explicit Phase A exclusion of questions answered correctly by every model.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same five Earth spheres, eight disciplines, 66 subfields, and captioning, MCQ, and open-ended tasks, including the same image configurations. The larger corpus and new studies use retained coverage; increased sample counts and the introduction of training experiments do not establish new domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2's main comparisons add Intern-S1-mini and the MSEarth-trained Qwen and Intern-S1 variants while retaining earlier models. Appendices J and K additionally evaluate human experts and o4-mini, including its reasoning-depth variants. These additions substantially extend comparisons to trained models and human performance.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a reported 441,785-example training set and post-training experiments, with training VQAs sampled 20% from Phase A and 80% from Phase B. New protocols include four experts judging 160 sampled open-ended questions, a three-expert performance baseline, and controlled CoT/reasoning-depth comparisons. The reported 7,195-item test size and existing caption-input ablation remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds human validation of the scoring metric (Appendix G.1), an expert baseline assessing benchmark difficulty (Appendix J), and reasoning-depth analysis with o4-mini (Appendix K). Post-training comparisons also test the generated data's utility. V1's caption ablation, case studies, and compute-scaling analysis remain; the latter moves to Appendix I.

E5.justification: V2 adds Krippendorff's alpha for annotator agreement, Spearman correlations with human judgments, and averaged scores from three human experts. These introduce statistical reporting for the new human studies, without adding confidence intervals, significance tests, or model-training seed and repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New results include Intern-S1-mini-MSEarth's 63.54% MCQ accuracy, versus 58.12% for its base model; human accuracy of 87.00%, versus 47.33–53.00% for compared models; metric correlations; and additional CoT outcomes (v2 Tables 2, 11, 13, 14). Earlier models' higher main-table MCQ scores reuse original-caption results already in v1 Table 10, rather than demonstrate new gains. V2 Table 8 also corrects an open-ended multi-image percentage from 45.1% to 54.9%.

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 introduces a discrete human-reference score: 1 when at least three of four annotators judge an answer correct, 0.5 for two, and 0 otherwise. This is a limited added mathematical scoring definition; no new theorems, proofs, or theoretical derivations appear.

C1.justification: V1 primarily contributes a graduate-level evaluation benchmark and construction framework. V2 explicitly contributes a training dataset alongside the benchmark, claims its effectiveness for post-training, and adds development of a state-of-the-art baseline to the introduction's contributions. The abstract and conclusion adopt this broader scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving an approximately 75% perception threshold, insufficient scientific pretraining, missing reasoning mechanisms, and benefits of domain-focused training (Section 4.3.1). Appendix K attributes variable CoT benefits to reasoning training and existing reasoning capability. It also interprets the new human studies, while removing v1's explicit limitation about underrepresented niche subfields.

D1.justification: V2 supplies training-data composition and sampling proportions, an Intern-S1-mini checkpoint path, explicit OpenDataLab/CC BY 4.0 provenance, and revised anonymous code and dataset access information, including a claim to release training code. It does not provide detailed post-training hyperparameters, hardware, budgets, or train/test separation procedures.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Intern-S1, DeepSeekMath for GRPO, and LAVE for human-based evaluator validation. Positioning broadens toward training resources, but the earlier scientific-benchmark comparisons largely remain. Changing citation style and relocating the benchmark comparison table do not constitute additional substantive changes.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and rewrites its motivation, contribution statements, and conclusion around a dataset-and-benchmark narrative. It replaces the main compute-scaling subsection with analysis and discussion, moves compute scaling into the appendices, reorganizes ethics material, removes the limitations section, and adds an editorial LLM-use disclosure and new analysis sections.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 3, and 4 are redrawn, including training-data outputs. V2 adds a train/test statistics summary and metric-validation, human-performance, and CoT tables, and expands the main result tables with trained-model rows. Existing benchmark comparisons, detailed test statistics, and the compute-scaling plot move, alongside document-wide typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful evidence absent from v1: human performance contextualizes benchmark difficulty, Table 11 checks evaluator agreement with human judgments, and post-training comparisons support the dataset's utility. The main MCQ table also consistently uses previously reported original-caption results. These gains are tempered by missing training and split details, stronger mechanism claims without isolating experiments, and removal of the coverage limitation. The net improvement is supported but limited.
